keyword: how long to get to the moon artemis 2

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a roughly 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R2: '10-day journey'; R3: '10-day mission'; R4: '10-day journey'; R6: '10 days'; R7: implied 10-day with launch April 1 to splashdown April 10.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state or imply approximately 10 days, with R1's 9.5 days fitting 'roughly'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will take approximately four to five days for the crew to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R2: 'Days 2-4: Outbound transit... Day 5-6: Lunar fly-by'; R5: 'Days 5-6: Arrival at the moon'; R7: 'The trip to the moon will take about four days.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe 4 days outbound after initial Earth orbit, aligning with 4-5 days to vicinity.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will perform a flyby of the Moon on the sixth day rather than entering lunar orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it'; R2: 'Day 6, the crew will come its closest... lunar fly-by'; R3: 'swing around, passing over the far side'; R5: 'get to the moon on the sixth day... one pass around the moon, never entering low-lunar orbit'; R6: 'Day 6: Lunar flyby day'.
verifications.reasoning: All confirm flyby (no orbit) specifically on day 6.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will fly around the far side of the Moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it, getting an unprecedented view of the far side'; R2: 'pass within approximately 4,100 miles beyond the far side'; R3: 'passing behind the moon... far side'; R4: 'whip around the lunar far side'; R5: 'trip around the “dark side of the moon”'; R6: 'swing around the moon'; R7: 'pass behind the leading edge of the moon... far side'.
verifications.reasoning: Unanimous confirmation of far-side flyby before return.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will perform a translunar injection burn on Day 2 to head toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first 24 hours... orbiting the Earth... Then... "trans-lunar injection," or TLI'; R2: 'Days 2 - 4: Outbound transit... translunar injection burn'; R5: 'translunar injection burn... on the second day'; R6: 'Day 2: ... “translunar injection burn”'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources place TLI after Day 1 Earth orbit, explicitly on Day 2 in R5/R6.

verifications.claim: On day 6, the Artemis II crew will fly about 4,000 nautical miles above the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'day 6... pass within approximately 4,100 miles beyond the far side'; R4: 'day six... as close as 4,000 miles'; R5: 'day 6... at least 4,000 nautical miles above the moon’s surface'; R7: 'about 4,100 miles of the lunar surface'.
verifications.reasoning: Day 6 closest approach ~4,000-4,100 miles; R5 uses 'nautical miles' matching claim exactly, others approximate.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is designed to test systems over a 10-day period.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule... check out the Orion capsule'; R2: 'testing its systems'; R3: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey'; R4: 'shakedown mission test-flying the Orion spacecraft'; R6: 'test the rocket and spacecraft'; R7: 'test flight... check out all of (Orion's) environmental control, life support systems'.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly a test mission over the ~10-day duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will return to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10'; R2: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10'; R6: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R7: 'Pacific Ocean splashdown off the Southern California coast'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II flight will take the crew farther from Earth than any human in history.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'travel farther from Earth than anyone before them'; R3: 'set a distance record... farthest that any humans have ever traveled from Earth'; R4: 'farther from Earth than any person has ever ventured'; R7: 'equaling and then surpassing a record set by the Apollo 13 crew'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements of new record distance.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II flight will reach over 252,000 miles away from Earth
verifications.label: CLEAR
